topic: Claim: the crew's scattering, not Ace's death, is what sent Luffy into two years of training
title: Why Luffy Really Trained For Two Years
description: Fans say Ace's death made Luffy stronger. I think the real trigger was the crew scattered at Sabaody. Here is my read, plus a full What If Ace Survived Marineford breakdown on the channel.
comment: What pushed Luffy harder: losing Ace or losing his crew? Pick one.

lines.text: Why did Luffy really train for two years after Marineford?

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text

lines.text: Most fans say Ace's death. After chapter 575, Luffy was shattered.

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text

lines.text: Law operated on him, and he woke on Amazon Lily wanting to give up.

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text

lines.text: That's the steelman, and it's strong. But look at what Luffy actually says.

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text

lines.text: He didn't just mourn Ace. He said he'd been too weak to protect anyone.

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text

lines.text: That weakness had two faces: Ace dying, and his crew being sent away by Kuma.

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text

lines.text: Rayleigh then trained him on Rusukaina for two years.

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text

lines.text: But the thing that sent him there was the promise to his crew at Sabaody.

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text

lines.text: So take Ace's death out, and I think Luffy still trains. The crew scatter still happens.

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text

lines.text: What changes is the weight he carries. Not the motive.

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text

lines.text: He'd be a happier Luffy, and maybe a more careless one.

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text

lines.text: That's why I keep asking: why did Luffy really train for two years?

shot.fallback: anime style dramatic pirate scene, no text
